blocks.text: Milder air is set to spread across the UK over the coming days, with temperatures climbing as high as 14C.
It will bring a marked contrast to recent days when cold air dominated, bringing overnight frosts and snow to some northern hills.
Whilst some north-eastern areas will remain chilly on Saturday, temperatures will rise more widely on Sunday and Monday.
This transition will be accompanied by outbreaks of rain, some of which will be heavy and persistent. It will also be rather windy with the possibility of gales in a few locations.
Soggy and blustery on Saturday
Outbreaks of heavy rain will spread from the west on Saturday as a developing weather system moves eastwards.

Almost all areas will see some wet weather but the highest rainfall totals are likely to occur across Wales and south-west England - where a few locations could see more than 30mm, especially over hills.
The rain will be accompanied by strong winds which could gust to 40-50mph around some exposed coasts.
This weather system will usher in some milder air from the west, with temperatures likely to peak at 14C in south-west England.
However, the cold air that has sat across the UK this week is stubborn and will be reluctant to clear.
Parts of central and southern Scotland, as well as northern and eastern England, will see afternoon highs of just 4-6C, remaining below the norm for this time of year.
Drier for many on Sunday
The wettest weather will clear during Saturday night leaving drier conditions on Sunday.
Some fog patches are possible first thing, especially in southern and eastern England, but these should clear and most parts of the UK will see a mix of patchy cloud and sunny spells.
Showers are also expected, particularly in Northern Ireland and Scotland where some could be heavy with hail and thunder, and accompanied by gusty winds.
Milder air will continue its journey across the country, lifting temperatures to 7-13C, much closer to the seasonal average.
Mild start to winter
Meteorological winter begins on 1 December but as we enter the coldest season of the year it looks like the weather will continue to turn milder.
By Tuesday temperatures are forecast to rise into double digits almost everywhere, ranging from 10-14C.
This milder weather will be accompanied by spells of rain, which is much-needed with large parts of the country in drought.
The rain will potentially be very heavy and persistent over hills in the west. It will also be windy at times, especially in the far north-west.
You can check the forecast for where you are on BBC Weather online or the app .
This change in weather type comes after what has been an unusually cold November.
According to the Met Office, temperatures across the UK as a whole are currently around 1.2C below the long-term norm.
If this continues until the end of November it will be the first month of below-average temperatures since January.
